question_text: What is the function of the codon AUG?

verification.note: Sourced from "Sr. Botany — My Baby Bullet-Q" (Sri Publishers, STAR-Q Pass Track), book p.44, printed question 101. insider_note: AUG has TWO functions. Both are needed, and 'initiation codon' plus 'methionine' is the whole answer.

steps.label: It starts translation
steps.margin_note: Say two functions first, then give the first one.
lines: 1. It acts as the INITIATION codon, or start
Translation begins at the AUG that starts the
steps.why: Every protein has to start somewhere, and a codon that marks the start is what sets the reading frame for everything after it.
common_mistakes: Calling AUG a stop codon. The stop codons are UAA, UAG and UGA.
Giving one function only. AUG has two.

steps.label: It codes for methionine
steps.margin_note: The second function, its consequence, and the term dual function.

lines.text: AUG starts the message AND codes for

lines: 2. It codes for the amino acid METHIONINE.
So every newly made protein begins with
methionine, though it is often removed later.
AUG is called a DUAL FUNCTION codon.
steps.why: Having one codon do both jobs is why every protein begins with the same amino acid, whatever it goes on to become.
common_mistakes: Naming a different amino acid. AUG codes for METHIONINE.
Saying the methionine always stays. It is often removed after translation.
steps.memory_tip: Start and methionine: two jobs, one codon.
